title: Governor of South Dakota

context.text: Incumbent Republican Larry Rhoden became governor in January 2025 when Kristi Noem resigned to become U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security; he was lieutenant governor from 2019 to 2025 and is seeking his first full term.

No Republican reached 35% in the June 2, 2026 primary, triggering South Dakota's first-ever gubernatorial runoff. Rhoden and retail and real estate executive Toby Doeden advanced; U.S. Rep. Dusty Johnson and House Speaker Jon Hansen were eliminated. Rhoden won the July 28 runoff with 70.8%.

Dan Ahlers, executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party and a former state legislator, is the Democratic nominee. The state's candidate list shows only the Republican and Democratic tickets for governor.

candidates.name: Larry Rhoden
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. Tony Venhuizen. Won the July 28, 2026 Republican runoff over Toby Doeden.

priorities.text: Keeping South Dakota strong, safe and free.
priorities.quote: I want to keep South Dakota safe – with low crime and respect for law enforcement.

priorities.text: Implementing property tax cuts, supporting rural health care and expanding defense manufacturing through the South Dakota Defense Institute.

record.text: Signed SB 245 on March 12, 2026, creating a state-backed fund for homeowner property tax relief.
Signed SB 96 on March 12, 2026, allowing counties to adopt a sales tax to offset property tax cuts.

candidates.researchNotes: No dedicated issue pages were found on his campaign site, and no direct source tying him to the fixed issue statements was gathered, so positions are omitted. His state Senate roll-call votes were not reviewed.

candidates.name: Dan Ahlers
candidates.ballotNote: Running with former state Rep. Steven McCleerey.
candidates.currentRole: Executive director, South Dakota Democratic Party

priorities.text: Education, small business, family farms and affordable health care, with a bipartisan approach.
priorities.quote: The truth is, no matter our party, we share the same core values.

priorities.text: Rural health care access and cost of living; said South Dakota does not need a state income tax, citing budget surpluses.

positions.summary: Says there is room for cooperation with federal immigration agents but criticizes heavy-handed tactics.
positions.quote: I don't like officers wearing masks.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign website (danahlers.com) was found and its issues page read; it lists goals but takes no explicit side on abortion, guns, school choice or other listed issues, so only statements are shown. Its wage line does not mention the minimum wage, so it is not shown. His old legislative service (2007-2011, 2017-2019) predates the repo's roll-call snapshots, and no individual bills or votes were gathered.
